name: Dinny-Mara

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The Irish and Scottish folkloric figure Dinny-Mara, also called Dooinney Marrey, names a male half-fish fairy of the sea. Most sea fairies were female, but literature records occasional mermen. The merman was rarely attractive. He had piggy eyes and a red nose from drinking brandy saved from wrecked ships. His breath smelled because he ate uncooked fish. The British historian Holinshed reported a merman captured alive in the reign of King John of England. People called him the Wild Man of Oxford, and he did not live long in captivity.

okr.objective: Record the male Merman form of Celtic sea fairies as Dinny-Mara.
